formats.key: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
effects: Sets the owners of a new Safe proxy to `_owners` and the signing threshold to `_threshold`. This is a one-time call: it reverts when the threshold is already set.
Sets `fallbackHandler` as the Safe's fallback handler when it is not zero.
Runs `data` as a DELEGATECALL to `to` inside the new Safe when `to` is not zero. This runs any code with the Safe's storage and balances.
Pays `payment` of `paymentToken` (zero address = ETH) from the Safe to `paymentReceiver`. When `paymentReceiver` is zero, tx.origin (the signer) receives it.
Called on the deployed singleton 0x41675C…, the call always reverts with GS200, because the constructor sets threshold = 1.
formats.shown: "Setup Safe" with the owners, the threshold, the fallback handler, the payment in its token, the payment receiver, and the delegate-call payload under the label "Module", decoded as a nested call.

findings.title: setup is bound to the Safe 1.4.1 singleton, where every call reverts; real Safe proxies never match.
findings.evidence: descriptor context.contract.deployments: only 0x41675C099F32341bf84BFc5382aF534df5C7461a on each chain. Safe.sol constructor: `threshold = 1;` OwnerManager.setupOwners: `require(threshold == 0, "GS200");`. Case 0: the mined tx 0x1b47aa… to the singleton has status 0 (reverted), and effects are empty.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies instead of the singleton. Use a `factory` constraint on SafeProxyFactory 1.4.1 with its ProxyCreation deployEvent, or match on the proxy's singleton.

findings.title: setup labels the delegate-call payload "Module" and never says it runs as a delegate call.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules: `require(execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, type(uint256).max), "GS000");`. Descriptor: `"path": "data", "label": "Module", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to"}`. Case 0: the reader believed "Module 0x29fcB43b… is enabled", but the payload is setupToL2(l2Singleton). No module is enabled.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Delegate call (runs in Safe)". Add a field for `to` labelled "Delegate call target".

findings.title: setup shows the zero address as payment receiver; the code then pays tx.origin, the signer.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Descriptor: the `paymentReceiver` field is addressName with no special value for zero.
findings.fix: Add `"senderAddress": "$.metadata.constants.addressAsNull"` to the paymentReceiver params, or a label that says zero means the transaction sender.

findings.title: The only setup test targets the singleton and reverts, so no real Safe setup is checked.
findings.evidence: Case 0: input.to = 0x41675c…, and mined.status = 0 with no effects.
findings.fix: Add a test from a SafeProxyFactory createProxyWithNonce transaction, with the initializer as the setup call on the proxy.

cases.notes: The mined tx reverted (status 0) because setup was sent to the singleton, where the threshold is already 1. The signer has no effects. The reader also wrongly thought a module would be enabled. The payload is setupToL2, which switches the Safe to the L2 singleton.

formats.key: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
effects: Sends msg.value native currency from the signer to the Safe. The function is payable.
Has the Safe CALL or DELEGATECALL `to` with `data` and `value` ETH from the Safe's balance, as `operation` says. A delegate call runs `to`'s code with the Safe's storage and balances.

Pays a refund of (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in `gasToken` (zero = ETH, capped at tx.gasprice) from the Safe to `refundReceiver`. When `refundReceiver` is zero, tx.origin receives it. The refund is paid even when the inner call fails, if safeTxGas or gasPrice is not zero.
Increases the Safe nonce. With a v=1 signature, the signer's own submission counts as their approval of the Safe transaction.
formats.shown: "sign multisig operation" with the operation type, the Safe, the executing signer, the decoded nested call, baseGas raw as "Gas amount", gasPrice as a token amount, and the refund receiver. msg.value, `value` and safeTxGas have no field.

findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.evidence: Safe.sol: `) public payable virtual returns (bool success) {` with no check that msg.value is zero. The descriptor execTransaction fields have no `@.value` field.

findings.title: execTransaction never shows the `value` ETH that the Safe sends to `to`. A plain ETH transfer shows no amount.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)`. The descriptor passes `value` only as `amountPath` of the `data` calldata field. Per the spec, a nested descriptor MAY use @.value. An empty or unmatched `data` gets only a hash.

findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to`, even when `operation` makes it a delegate call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute runs delegatecall when operation == DelegateCall. Descriptor: `"path": "data", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to", ...}` has no condition on `operation`.
findings.fix: Show the nested calldata only when operation is Call. For operation 1, show a fixed warning such as "Delegate call: runs target code inside your Safe". Or limit nested decoding to known delegate-call targets such as MultiSend.

findings.title: execTransaction says "sign multisig operation", but it executes the operation and can pay a refund.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `"intent": "sign multisig operation"`. Safe.execTransaction runs execute(...) and then handlePayment(...).
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction".

findings.title: execTransaction shows the gas price and baseGas apart and never shows the total refund the Safe pays.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`. Descriptor: baseGas is labelled 'Gas amount' (raw) and gasPrice 'Gas price' (tokenAmount). safeTxGas has visible: never.
findings.fix: Rename baseGas to "Base gas (refunded)" and gasPrice to "Refund per gas unit". Make safeTxGas visible as "Safe Tx gas".

findings.title: execTransaction shows a zero refundReceiver as the zero address; the code pays tx.origin.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver`. Descriptor: refundReceiver is addressName with no senderAddress.

findings.title: execTransaction is bound to the singleton; signers call Safe proxies, so this format never matches.
findings.evidence: deployments: only 0x41675C… The singleton has no owners, so checkNSignatures always fails with GS026.
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies with a factory constraint on SafeProxyFactory.

effects: Adds `owner` as a Safe owner. The function is `authorized`: only the Safe itself can call it, through execTransaction.
Sets the threshold to `_threshold` when it differs from the current one.
formats.shown: "Add signer" with the new signer and the new threshold.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold binds to the singleton; as a nested call the callee is the proxy, so it never matches.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold is `public authorized` (msg.sender == address(this)). The only deployment is singleton 0x41675C…
findings.fix: Bind to Safe proxies, which is the callee when execTransaction calls the Safe itself.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold limits the owner to type eoa, but owners can be contracts such as nested Safes.
findings.evidence: Descriptor owner params: `"types": ["eoa"]`. OwnerManager only rejects address(0), the sentinel and address(this).

Sets the threshold to `_threshold` when it differs from the current one.

effects: Sets the number of owner confirmations the Safe needs to `_threshold`. Only the Safe itself can call it.

effects: Records the signer, who must be an owner, as approving the Safe transaction hash `hashToApprove`. The approval is permanent and cannot be revoked. Anyone can then execute that Safe transaction with the signer's approval counted.
formats.shown: "Approve Safe hash" with the raw hash.

findings.title: approveHash shows only a hash; the Safe transaction it approves cannot be decoded from it.
findings.evidence: Safe.approveHash: `approvedHashes[msg.sender][hashToApprove] = 1;` The devdoc says "The approved hash stays approved forever. There's no revocation mechanism". Descriptor: hashToApprove is raw.
findings.fix: Change the intent to say it is permanent, for example "Approve Safe tx hash (permanent)".

findings.title: approveHash binds to the singleton; owners call it on their Safe proxy, so it never matches.
findings.evidence: Safe.approveHash: `require(owners[msg.sender] != address(0), "GS030");`. The singleton has no owners. The only deployment is 0x41675C…

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.reason: No path reverts on a non-zero msg.value, so ETH the signer sends stays in the Safe. The amount is never shown. This matches the guide's example of a payable function with no `@.value` and nothing forcing it to zero.
findings.quote: Safe.sol execTransaction: `) public payable virtual returns (bool success) {`. Nothing in the body reads or checks msg.value, and execute() forwards the `value` argument, not msg.value. Descriptor execTransaction fields: operation, @.to, @.from, data, baseGas, gasPrice, refundReceiver, safeTxGas, signatures. There is no `@.value`.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction never shows the `value` ETH that the Safe sends to `to`. A plain ETH transfer shows no amount.
findings.reason: The Safe sends `value` ETH to `to`, and no field in the format shows it. For a plain ETH transfer, `data` is empty and no nested descriptor exists, so the amount never appears. Not-critical case 5 does not apply, because the amount is not shown anywhere else.
findings.quote: Executor.execute: `success := call(txGas, to, value, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0)`. Descriptor: the `data` field uses format `calldata` with `"amountPath": "value"`, and no field has path `value`. The spec says the nested descriptor 'MAY reference this value using the `@.value` container path'. If no descriptor is found, the wallet 'MAY display a hash of the embedded calldata instead'.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction decodes `data` as a call to `to`, even when `operation` makes it a delegate call.
findings.reason: When operation is 1, the nested data still renders as a normal call to `to`, but the code runs `to`'s code inside the Safe, so the outcome shown does not happen. The 'Operation type' field shows 'Delegate Call', but the guide lists this exact pattern as critical even with `operation` present.
findings.quote: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`. Descriptor: `"path": "data", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}`, with no condition on `operation`.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.

findings.title: execTransaction never shows the `value` ETH that the Safe sends to `to`. A plain ETH transfer shows no amount.
